messages:
elaine: Heads-up — customer acct `acme-corp` opened an escalation. They downloaded an audit export for 2026-02-10 and flagged two things: (1) several `kms_key_id` fields in the export they weren't expecting, and (2) a handful of API 5xx/504 errors around 09:12 UTC the same day. They want clarity on what the export includes, whether any secrets are in scope, and who can see KMS/HSM metadata. cc @jamie for security guidance.

samir: Got it. Do we have the exact export file or a snippet? Also can you paste the timeline for the 5xxs? I can start a repro.

elaine: Customer attached a CSV (I downloaded locally). Sample log lines: 
```
2026-02-10T09:11:58Z, request_id=abc123, user_id=uid-55, action=ModelInference, status=200, kms_key_id=redwood:k-7f3e
2026-02-10T09:12:03Z, request_id=abc124, user_id=uid-55, action=ModelInference, status=504, error="upstream timeout"
2026-02-10T09:12:07Z, request_id=abc125, user_id=uid-55, action=Embedding, status=200, kms_key_id=redwood:k-7f3e
```
I removed some columns but the CSV includes `kms_key_id` column for a subset of rows.

samir: Thanks. Repro steps I'll try: 
```
# export command customer used (internal export tool)
export-cli --tenant acme-corp --from 2026-02-10T00:00:00Z --to 2026-02-11T00:00:00Z --format csv > acme-audit.csv
```
Will run against staging to confirm shape.

maria: Quick note from support-bot: case #2468 created and customer notified we've escalated to security + infra. They asked for an ETA within 24h.

jamie: Initial sec guidance: KMS key IDs in logs are identifiers only — they do not contain key material or plaintext. HSMs never leak raw keys in logs. That said, we need to confirm whether any other fields in the export could contain sensitive payloads (e.g., request bodies or embeddings) for this tenant.

elaine: Understood. Customer specifically worried we exported any request payloads or embedding vectors. The CSV header shows columns: timestamp, request_id, user_id, action, status, latency_ms, kms_key_id, route. No `request_body` or `embedding_vector` columns present.

jamie: OK that's good. Still want infra to confirm the export pipeline scrubs bodies by default. @ops-bot can you run the dataflow check for export-sanitizer v2?

ops-bot: dataflow-check triggered: export-sanitizer v2 — last run 2026-02-10T02:03:12Z, ruleset: default-scrub-v3. No rule violations detected for tenant acme-corp in that run.

samir: I ran the export-cli on staging with the same flags. Output schema matches their CSV and contains `kms_key_id` only as an ID string. No bodies. I also replayed a subset of traffic around 09:12 and saw a transient upstream timeout on a specific backend shard — looks like a routing flake causing 504s.

jamie: Two action items: (A) Confirm export pipeline scrubbing for historical exports (not just latest run). (B) Provide a tight, written answer to customer explaining KMS/HSM metadata exposure is limited to key identifiers and no secret material was present. We should include a short technical note on the export sanitizer ruleset and the 504s being unrelated to KMS.

elaine: I'll draft the reply. Proposed timeline: verify historical exports within 48 hrs, share a customer-facing statement within 24 hrs confirming nothing sensitive included, and follow up with a longer post-mortem for the 5xxs within 72 hrs. Legal wants to review the customer statement before it goes out.

maria: Legal looped in (we've added legal@redwood). Customer accepted 24h ETA for the initial reassurance.

samir: For the 504s I can open a separate incident and include traces. Quick repro: call the inference endpoint with model=simple-embed and a 2s client timeout; ramp parallel requests to reproduce 504s on the same backend shard. I'll include sampling of request_ids (abc124, abc126, abc129) in the incident.

jamie: Also note: if customer asks who has access to KMS metadata internally, provide roles: infra-admins and sec-lambda service account have read-only visibility for identifiers in logs; no human can retrieve key material without HSM unseal operations and proper change control. We can attach an access-control screenshot from the audit console.

elaine: Sounds good. Next updates here: I'll post the legal-approved customer message and the historical-export check results. If anyone hits blockers with infra checks ping me. :eyes: 

ops-bot: remind set for 24h — follow up in #incidents at 2026-02-11T09:00:00Z.

maria: Thanks all. Customer is breathing easier now that we confirmed there's no request payload column. I'll keep the case open until closure. :white_check_mark:
